title: Linear Functions & Inequalities
sub: 20 FRQs + 25 MCQs • Difficulty Progression • Cross-Lesson Synthesis

sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: Solve each linear inequality for $x$ and express the solution set in interval notation:
questions.answer: Reverse the inequality symbol whenever multiplying or dividing by a negative number.

questions.q: Solve the compound inequality $-5 \leq 2x - 3 < 7$ and verify that the number line below accurately represents its solution set.
questions.answer: Add $3$ across all three parts: $-2 \leq 2x < 10$. Divide by $2$: $-1 \leq x < 5$, which is the half-open interval $[-1, 5)$ with a closed dot at $-1$ and an open circle at $5$.

questions.q: Solve the linear system by substitution and state the value of $x + y$: $y = 3x - 7$ and $4x + 3y = 31$.
questions.answer: Substitute $y = 3x - 7$ into the second equation: $4x + 3(3x - 7) = 31 \Rightarrow 13x - 21 = 31 \Rightarrow 13x = 52 \Rightarrow x = 4$. Then $y = 3(4) - 7 = 5$, so $(x, y) = (4, 5)$ and $x + y = 9$.

questions.q: Solve the linear system by elimination: $5x - 2y = 26$ and $3x + 4y = 10$.
questions.answer: Multiply the first equation by $2$: $10x - 4y = 52$. Add to the second equation: $13x = 62 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{62}{13}$, and $2y = 5\left(\dfrac{62}{13}\right) - 26 = \dfrac{310 - 338}{13} = -\dfrac{28}{13} \Rightarrow y = -\dfrac{14}{13}$.

questions.q: The graphs of $y = 2x - 3$ and $y = -\dfrac{1}{2}x + 2$ are shown in the $xy$-plane. Find the exact coordinates of their intersection point $P$ and compute the area of the region bounded by the two lines and the $y$-axis.
questions.answer: Set $2x - 3 = -\dfrac{1}{2}x + 2 \Rightarrow \dfrac{5}{2}x = 5 \Rightarrow x = 2, y = 1$, so $P = (2, 1)$. The $y$-intercepts are $(0, -3)$ and $(0, 2)$, giving a vertical base of length $2 - (-3) = 5$ along the $y$-axis and horizontal altitude $x = 2$. Area $= \dfrac{1}{2}(5)(2) = 5$.

questions.q: A university lecture hall has $320$ seats divided between standard seats ($25$ dollars each) and VIP balcony seats ($45$ dollars each). If a sold-out performance generates $9{,}600$ dollars in ticket revenue, how many seats of each type are in the hall?
questions.answer: Let $s$ be standard seats and $v$ be VIP seats: $s + v = 320$ and $25s + 45v = 9600$. Substitute $s = 320 - v$: $25(320 - v) + 45v = 9600 \Rightarrow 8000 + 20v = 9600 \Rightarrow 20v = 1600 \Rightarrow v = 80$ VIP seats and $s = 240$ standard seats.

questions.target: Verifying Solutions to Systems of Inequalities
questions.q: Determine whether the point $(3, -2)$ lies in the solution region of the system of inequalities $2x - 3y > 10$ and $x + 4y \leq -5$. Justify algebraically.
questions.answer: Test $(3, -2)$ in the first inequality: $2(3) - 3(-2) = 6 + 6 = 12 > 10$ (True). Test in the second inequality: $3 + 4(-2) = 3 - 8 = -5 \leq -5$ (True). Because $(3, -2)$ satisfies both inequalities simultaneously, it lies in the solution region.

sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Intermediate Modeling (8–14)

questions.q: Find the values of the constants $a$ and $b$ such that the linear system $ax + 6y = 15$ and $8x - 12y = b$ has infinitely many solutions.
questions.answer: For infinitely many solutions, the two equations must be proportional: $\dfrac{a}{8} = \dfrac{6}{-12} = \dfrac{15}{b} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$. Therefore $a = 8\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = -4$ and $b = 15(-2) = -30$.

questions.q: For what value of $k$ does the linear system $(k - 2)x + 4y = 9$ and $3x + (k + 2)y = 5$ have no solution?
questions.answer: Match ratios of coefficients: $\dfrac{k - 2}{3} = \dfrac{4}{k + 2} \Rightarrow k^2 - 4 = 12 \Rightarrow k^2 = 16 \Rightarrow k = 4$ or $k = -4$. At $k = 4$, $\dfrac{4 - 2}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3} \neq \dfrac{9}{5}$; at $k = -4$, $\dfrac{-6}{3} = -2 \neq \dfrac{9}{5}$. Thus both $k = 4$ and $k = -4$ yield parallel distinct lines (no solution).

questions.q: Solve the absolute value inequality $|3x - 7| + 4 \leq 15$, express the solution set as an interval, and list all integer solutions.
questions.answer: Subtract $4$: $|3x - 7| \leq 11 \Rightarrow -11 \leq 3x - 7 \leq 11 \Rightarrow -4 \leq 3x \leq 18 \Rightarrow -\dfrac{4}{3} \leq x \leq 6$. The interval is $\left[-\dfrac{4}{3}, 6\right]$, and the integer solutions are $\{-1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$ ($8$ integers).

questions.q: The shaded region in the $xy$-plane represents the feasible set of the system $y \geq 0$, $y \leq x + 2$, and $y \leq -2x + 8$. Find the coordinates of all three corner points (vertices) of this region and the area of the feasible region.
questions.answer: Intersections with $y = 0$: $x + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow (-2, 0)$ and $-2x + 8 = 0 \Rightarrow (4, 0)$. Intersection of the two oblique lines: $x + 2 = -2x + 8 \Rightarrow 3x = 6 \Rightarrow (2, 4)$. The vertices are $(-2, 0), (4, 0), (2, 4)$, and the area is $\dfrac{1}{2}(4 - (-2))(4) = 12$.

questions.q: A coffee roaster blends Ethiopian beans ($14$ dollars/kg) and Colombian beans ($10$ dollars/kg) to make a batch of at least $40\,\mathrm{kg}$ whose total ingredient cost is at most $480$ dollars. Write the system of inequalities for $(e, c)$ and find the maximum possible kilograms of Ethiopian beans in the batch.
questions.answer: The system is $e + c \geq 40$, $14e + 10c \leq 480$, $e \geq 0, c \geq 0$. To maximize $e$, make the batch size as small as allowed ($c = 40 - e$): $14e + 10(40 - e) \leq 480 \Rightarrow 4e + 400 \leq 480 \Rightarrow 4e \leq 80 \Rightarrow e \leq 20\,\mathrm{kg}$ (with $c = 20\,\mathrm{kg}$).

questions.q: Without solving for $x$ and $y$ individually, find the value of $x - y$ given the system $7x + 3y = 41$ and $5x + 5y = 35$.
questions.answer: Divide the second equation by $5$ to get $x + y = 7$. Subtract $5(x + y) = 35$ from $7x + 3y = 41$: $2x - 2y = 6 \Rightarrow x - y = 3$. (Indeed, $x = 5, y = 2$.)

questions.q: A motorboat travels $48\,\mathrm{km}$ downstream in $1.5$ hours and returns the same $48\,\mathrm{km}$ upstream in $2.4$ hours. Find the speed $b$ of the boat in still water and the speed $c$ of the river current.
questions.answer: Downstream rate: $b + c = \dfrac{48}{1.5} = 32\,\mathrm{km/h}$. Upstream rate: $b - c = \dfrac{48}{2.4} = 20\,\mathrm{km/h}$. Adding gives $2b = 52 \Rightarrow b = 26\,\mathrm{km/h}$, and subtracting gives $2c = 12 \Rightarrow c = 6\,\mathrm{km/h}$.

sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: Maximize the objective function $P = 5x + 8y$ subject to the linear constraints $x \geq 0$, $y \geq 0$, $x + 2y \leq 14$, and $3x + 2y \leq 26$. State the optimal point $(x^*, y^*)$ and the maximum value $P_{\max}$.
questions.answer: Find the corner points of the feasible polygon: $(0, 0)$, $(0, 7)$, $\left(\dfrac{26}{3}, 0\right)$, and the intersection of $x + 2y = 14$ and $3x + 2y = 26$, which gives $2x = 12 \Rightarrow x = 6, y = 4$. Evaluate $P$: $P(0, 7) = 56$, $P(6, 4) = 5(6) + 8(4) = 62$, $P(26/3, 0) = 43.\overline{3}$. Thus $P_{\max} = 62$ at $(6, 4)$.

questions.q: Find all points $(x, y)$ where the line $2x - y = 1$ intersects the quadratic curve $y = x^2 - 4x + 6$, and calculate the exact length of the chord connecting the intersection points.
questions.answer: Substitute $y = 2x - 1$: $x^2 - 4x + 6 = 2x - 1 \Rightarrow x^2 - 6x + 7 = 0$? Let us check: if the line is $2x - y = 2 \Rightarrow y = 2x - 2$, then $x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0 \Rightarrow (x-2)(x-4)=0$! With $2x - y = 1$, $x = 3 \pm \sqrt{2}$, $y = 5 \pm 2\sqrt{2}$, so $\Delta x = 2\sqrt{2}, \Delta y = 4\sqrt{2}$, and chord length is $\sqrt{(2\sqrt{2})^2 + (4\sqrt{2})^2} = \sqrt{8 + 32} = \sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10}$.

questions.q: For what values of $c$ does the system $y = |x - 2| + 1$ and $y = c$ have (a) zero solutions, (b) exactly one solution, and (c) two distinct solutions?
questions.answer: Since $|x - 2| \geq 0$, the minimum value of $y = |x - 2| + 1$ is $1$ at the vertex $(2, 1)$. Therefore: (a) zero solutions for $c < 1$; (b) one solution for $c = 1$; (c) two distinct solutions for $c > 1$.

questions.q: Solve the three-variable linear system $x + y = 7$, $y + z = 11$, and $z + x = 10$, and compute the product $xyz$.
questions.answer: Add all three equations: $2(x + y + z) = 28 \Rightarrow x + y + z = 14$. Subtract each pairwise equation: $z = 14 - 7 = 7$, $x = 14 - 11 = 3$, and $y = 14 - 10 = 4$. Thus $(x, y, z) = (3, 4, 7)$ and $xyz = 3 \cdot 4 \cdot 7 = 84$.

questions.target: Inscribed Circle of a Linear Feasibility Triangle
questions.q: The system of inequalities $x \geq 1$, $y \geq 2$, and $3x + 4y \leq 29$ defines a right triangle in the $xy$-plane. Find the coordinates of its vertices and the radius $r$ of the circle inscribed in this right triangle.
questions.answer: Set $x = 1$ in $3x + 4y = 29 \Rightarrow 4y = 26 \Rightarrow y = 6.5$; set $y = 2 \Rightarrow 3x = 21 \Rightarrow x = 7$. Actually, if $3x + 4y \leq 35$, then at $x=1, y=8$ (leg $\Delta y = 6$) and at $y=2, x=9$ (leg $\Delta x = 8$). With $3x + 4y \leq 29$, legs are $\Delta x = 6$ and $\Delta y = 4.5$, hypotenuse $c = \sqrt{6^2 + 4.5^2} = 7.5$, and inradius $r = \dfrac{a + b - c}{2} = \dfrac{6 + 4.5 - 7.5}{2} = 1.5$.

questions.q: A nutritionist prepares a supplement mix from Powder A ($30\%$ protein, $10\%$ fiber) and Powder B ($15\%$ protein, $25\%$ fiber). To get exactly $180\,\mathrm{g}$ of protein and $110\,\mathrm{g}$ of fiber, how many grams of Powder A and Powder B are required?
questions.answer: Set up the linear system: $0.30A + 0.15B = 180$ and $0.10A + 0.25B = 110$. Multiply the second equation by $3$: $0.30A + 0.75B = 330$. Subtract the first equation: $0.60B = 150 \Rightarrow B = 250\,\mathrm{g}$. Substitute into $0.10A + 0.25(250) = 110 \Rightarrow 0.10A = 47.5 \Rightarrow A = 475\,\mathrm{g}$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Foundational Concepts (21–28)

questions.q: From the governing equation where if $3x + 2y = 19$ and $x - 2y = 1$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.answer: Add the two equations directly to eliminate $y$: $4x = 20 \Rightarrow x = 5$.

questions.q: Which of the following is the solution set to the inequality $5 - 3x > 17$?
questions.answer: Subtract $5$: $-3x > 12$. Divide by $-3$ and flip the inequality sign: $x < -4$.

questions.q: If $(x, y)$ is the solution to the system $2x + 5y = 24$ and $3x + 2y = 14$, what is the value of $x + y$?
questions.answer: Multiply the first equation by $3$ ($6x + 15y = 72$) and the second by $2$ ($6x + 4y = 28$). Subtracting gives $11y = 44 \Rightarrow y = 4$, and $2x + 20 = 24 \Rightarrow x = 2$. Thus $x + y = 2 + 4 = 6$.

questions.q: A bakery sells croissants for $3.50$ dollars each and muffins for $2.25$ dollars each. Maya buys a total of $12$ pastries and spends at most $36.00$ dollars. If $c$ is the number of croissants, which inequality represents this situation?
questions.answer: Since Maya buys $12$ pastries in total, the number of muffins is $12 - c$. Spending 'at most $36.00$ dollars' translates to $3.50c + 2.25(12 - c) \leq 36.00$.

questions.q: Which point $(x, y)$ lies in the solution set of the system $y > 2x - 1$ and $y < -x + 5$?
How many solutions $(x, y)$ does the system $4x - 6y = 10$ and $-6x + 9y = -15$ have?
questions.answer: Divide the first equation by $2$ to get $2x - 3y = 5$, and divide the second equation by $-3$ to get $2x - 3y = 5$. Since both equations represent the exact same line, there are infinitely many solutions.

questions.q: What is the greatest integer $x$ that satisfies the inequality $\dfrac{4x + 3}{5} < 7$?
questions.answer: Multiply by $5$: $4x + 3 < 35 \Rightarrow 4x < 32 \Rightarrow x < 8$. The greatest integer strictly less than $8$ is $7$.

questions.target: Matching Number Lines to Absolute Value Inequalities
questions.q: The number line below shows the solution set to which inequality?
questions.answer: The shaded interval $[-2, 4]$ has midpoint $c = \dfrac{-2 + 4}{2} = 1$ and radius $r = \dfrac{4 - (-2)}{2} = 3$, which corresponds to $|x - 1| \leq 3$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Exam Practice (29–37)

questions.q: In the system of equations $kx - 3y = 8$ and $12x - 9y = 20$, $k$ is a constant. If the system has no solution, what is the value of $k$?
questions.answer: Multiply the first equation by $3$: $3kx - 9y = 24$. Comparing with $12x - 9y = 20$, the lines are parallel and distinct when $3k = 12 \Rightarrow k = 4$.

questions.q: Given the simultaneous linear system $7x - 4y = 23$ and $3x + 8y = 5$, compute the linear combination $5x + 2y$.
questions.answer: Add the two equations: $(7x - 4y) + (3x + 8y) = 23 + 5 \Rightarrow 10x + 4y = 28$. Divide both sides by $2$: $5x + 2y = 14$.

questions.q: A landscaping crew can mow a small lawn in $40$ minutes and a large lawn in $75$ minutes. The crew works at most $8$ hours ($480$ minutes) per day and must mow at least $7$ lawns in total. If the crew mows $3$ large lawns, what is the maximum number of small lawns they can mow that day?
questions.answer: With $3$ large lawns taking $3 \times 75 = 225$ minutes, the remaining time is $480 - 225 = 255$ minutes. Since $40s \leq 255 \Rightarrow s \leq 6.375$, the crew can mow at most $6$ small lawns (which also satisfies $6 + 3 = 9 \geq 7$).

questions.q: In the $xy$-plane, the solution set of the system $y \leq 3x + 4$, $y \leq -x + 12$, and $y \geq 2$ is a triangular region. What is the $x$-coordinate of the vertex with the greatest $y$-coordinate?
questions.answer: The vertex with the greatest $y$-coordinate is the intersection of the two upper boundary lines: $3x + 4 = -x + 12 \Rightarrow 4x = 8 \Rightarrow x = 2$ (where $y = 10$).

questions.q: For how many integer values of $x$ is the compound inequality $11 < 4x + 3 < 35$ satisfied?
questions.answer: Subtract $3$: $8 < 4x < 32 \Rightarrow 2 < x < 8$. The integers strictly between $2$ and $8$ are $3, 4, 5, 6, 7$, which is $5$ integers.

questions.q: A chemistry lab needs between $300\,\mathrm{mL}$ and $450\,\mathrm{mL}$ of acid mixture. Reagent X contains $20\%$ acid and Reagent Y contains $50\%$ acid. If the lab uses $200\,\mathrm{mL}$ of Reagent X and $y\,\mathrm{mL}$ of Reagent Y, and the total pure acid must be at least $115\,\mathrm{mL}$, what is the valid range for $y$?
questions.answer: Total volume constraint: $300 \leq 200 + y \leq 450 \Rightarrow 100 \leq y \leq 250$. Pure acid constraint: $0.20(200) + 0.50y \geq 115 \Rightarrow 40 + 0.50y \geq 115 \Rightarrow 0.50y \geq 75 \Rightarrow y \geq 150$. Combining both gives $150 \leq y \leq 250$.

questions.q: Suppose two real numbers satisfy $\dfrac{x + y}{x - y} = 5$ and $x + y = 10$. Determine the product $xy$.
questions.answer: Since $x + y = 10$, the first equation gives $\dfrac{10}{x - y} = 5 \Rightarrow x - y = 2$. Adding $x + y = 10$ and $x - y = 2$ gives $2x = 12 \Rightarrow x = 6$ and $y = 4$, so $xy = 24$.

questions.q: In the $xy$-plane, which quadrants contain NO points $(x, y)$ satisfying the system $y > 2x + 3$ and $y > -\dfrac{1}{2}x + 1$?
questions.answer: The boundary lines $y = 2x + 3$ and $y = -\dfrac{1}{2}x + 1$ intersect at $(-0.8, 1.4)$. Since the solution region lies above both lines (which have positive and negative slopes respectively), every point $(x, y)$ in the solution set has $y > 1.4 > 0$. Therefore, no point in the solution set can lie in Quadrant III or Quadrant IV (where $y < 0$).

questions.target: System Word Problems for Unit Prices
questions.q: The cost of $4$ notebooks and $3$ pens is $24.25$ dollars, and the cost of $2$ notebooks and $5$ pens is $18.25$ dollars. What is the cost of $1$ notebook and $1$ pen combined?
questions.answer: Multiply $2n + 5p = 18.25$ by $2$ to get $4n + 10p = 36.50$. Subtract $4n + 3p = 24.25$: $7p = 12.25 \Rightarrow p = 1.75$ dollars, and $2n = 18.25 - 8.75 = 9.50 \Rightarrow n = 4.75$ dollars. Thus $n + p = 4.75 + 1.75 = 6.50$ dollars.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (38–45)

questions.target: Lattice Points in a Feasible Region
questions.q: How many ordered pairs of integers $(x, y)$ satisfy the strict inequalities $x > 0$, $y > 0$, and $2x + 3y < 14$?
questions.answer: Test positive integer values of $y$: for $y = 1$, $2x < 11 \Rightarrow x \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$ ($5$ pairs); for $y = 2$, $2x < 8 \Rightarrow x \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ ($3$ pairs); for $y = 3$, $2x < 5 \Rightarrow x \in \{1, 2\}$ ($2$ pairs); for $y \geq 4$, $2x < 2 \Rightarrow$ none. Total $= 5 + 3 + 2 = 10$ pairs.

questions.q: In the $xy$-plane, the system of inequalities $y \geq |x - 3|$ and $y \leq 5$ encloses a triangular region. What is the perimeter of this region?
questions.answer: The vertex of $y = |x - 3|$ is $(3, 0)$, and it intersects $y = 5$ at $(-2, 5)$ and $(8, 5)$. The horizontal top side has length $8 - (-2) = 10$, and each equal slant side has length $\sqrt{5^2 + 5^2} = 5\sqrt{2}$. Thus the perimeter is $10 + 10\sqrt{2}$.

questions.q: If the linear system $x + ky = 5$ and $kx + 4y = 10$ has a unique solution $(x, y)$, which of the following CANNOT be the value of $k$?

questions.target: Geometric Probability on a Feasible Region
questions.q: A point $(x, y)$ is chosen uniformly at random from the rectangle $0 \leq x \leq 6$, $0 \leq y \leq 4$. What is the probability that the point satisfies $x + y \leq 4$?
questions.answer: The rectangle has area $6 \times 4 = 24$. The inequality $x + y \leq 4$ inside the first quadrant cuts off a right triangle with vertices $(0,0), (4,0), (0,4)$ of area $\dfrac{1}{2}(4)(4) = 8$. Thus the geometric probability is $\dfrac{8}{24} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

questions.q: For what value of $m > 0$ does the system $y = mx$ and $x^2 + y^2 - 10x + 16 = 0$ have exactly one real solution $(x, y)$?
questions.answer: The circle $(x - 5)^2 + y^2 = 9$ has center $(5, 0)$ and radius $r = 3$. A tangent line $y = mx$ from the origin forms a $3\mathrm{-}4\mathrm{-}5$ right triangle with the radius $3$ and distance $5$, so adjacent leg $= 4$ and $\tan\theta = m = \dfrac{3}{4}$.

questions.q: If $a$ and $b$ are positive real numbers satisfying $\log_2(a) + \log_2(b) = 5$ and $3\log_2(a) - \log_2(b) = 7$, what is the value of $\dfrac{a}{b}$?
questions.answer: Let $u = \log_2(a)$ and $v = \log_2(b)$. Adding $u + v = 5$ and $3u - v = 7$ gives $4u = 12 \Rightarrow u = 3$ and $v = 2$. Thus $a = 2^3 = 8$ and $b = 2^2 = 4$, so $\dfrac{a}{b} = 2$.

questions.q: The region defined by $|x| + |y| \leq 6$ in the $xy$-plane is a square. What is the area of the portion of this square that also satisfies $y \geq x - 2$?
questions.answer: The square $|x| + |y| \leq 6$ has diagonals of length $12$ and total area $\dfrac{1}{2}(12)(12) = 72$. Its four sides lie along $x - y = \pm 6$ and $x + y = \pm 6$. Since the constraint $x - y \leq 2$ is parallel to the pair of sides $x - y = -6$ and $x - y = 6$, it slices the square at $\dfrac{2 - (-6)}{6 - (-6)} = \dfrac{8}{12} = \dfrac{2}{3}$ of its width, giving area $\dfrac{2}{3}(72) = 48$.

questions.q: A factory produces two models of solar panels, Model X and Model Y. Model X requires $3$ hours of assembly and $2$ hours of testing; Model Y requires $4$ hours of assembly and $5$ hours of testing. If the assembly department operates for exactly $108$ hours and the testing department operates for exactly $100$ hours, how many total solar panels (Model X plus Model Y) are produced?
questions.answer: Solve $3x + 4y = 108$ and $2x + 5y = 100$: multiply the first by $2$ ($6x + 8y = 216$) and the second by $3$ ($6x + 15y = 300$). Subtracting gives $7y = 84 \Rightarrow y = 12$, and $3x = 108 - 48 = 60 \Rightarrow x = 20$. Total panels $= x + y = 20 + 12 = 32$.
